p: Tasty falafel and other mideastern food. Prepare for long queues.

Lounge in a former locomotive construction hall (1930s style), mix of after work crowd and normal scene.

A small cafe that takes coffee very seriously. Or, to say it in their words: "Please be aware that we have certain preferences when serving a coffee the way we believe it tastes best." Children are not really welcome, there is only a…
Best grill restaurant in town with divine steaks and fresh oysters. Reservation for every night is essential.

Millions of visitors leaving East Berlin by train said tearful goodbyes to their friends and relatives from the East at this former border checkpoint. Hardly a year after the wall came down, the building was turned into a nightclub…

Built 1859-1866 this is one of the most architecturally stunning synagogues in Germany to survive both the Nazi era and the war.

The museum’s treasures include the sculpture collection with works of art from the middle ages to the 18th century. The Bode museum is best known for its Byzantine art collection and the coin cabinet.

This retro-style bar with its orange waiting room seats is a popular and often crowded venue for watching all important football games on multiple large projection screens, for dancing and for playing kicker.
Vegetarian Vietnamese family restaurant, many dishes are Vegan.

Specializes in 19th-century painting and sculpture; Monet, Manet, Cézanne, C. David Friedrich and other important 18th- and 19th-century artists are well-represented.

There are three huge collections housed within this grand building: the Collection of Classical Antiquities, the Museum of Near Eastern Antiquities and the Museum of Islamic Art. The Pergamon Museum was the last museum built on…

Pays tribute to the Punk band The Ramones. It displays more than 300 unique and original Ramones memorabilia. You can get a drink at cafe Mania inside the museum. DeeDee Ramone grew up in Berlin and the city is mentioned in several of…

This chapel was built on the site of a church built in 1894 which sat on the "death strip" and was thus blown up by the GDR authorities in 1985. The chapel is the site of occasional memorial services for victims of the wall.
Four floors of exhibitions with a relatively good variety of genres and artists. A very nice oasis of calm from the busy Friedrichstraße.
One of the most famous German art galleries, home to the Neue Leipziger Schule (Neo Rauch et al.)
Contemporary theatre. The theater was founded by Bertolt Brecht after the war in what was then East Berlin.
Classical theater with impressive line up of actors and directors. Some events have English subtitles.
Cabaret and comedy, political satire in German. Their home venue is in the Admiralspalast.
Berlin's biggest show with over 100 artists on the biggest theater stage in the world.
In Riverside Hotel next to the Friedrichstadtpalast.
Good French cuisine direct at the terrace of the river and close to the theaters.
Famous basement restaurant in former house of Brecht with Austrian inspired kitchen (receipts from Helene Weigel), reservations essential!
Vegan restaurant with upmarket touch that specialises in rather typical German dishes like Roulade or Cordon Bleu that Vegans would normally not eat. Weekend brunch from 09:30 - 16:00.

Italian family restaurant where supposedly stars like Brad Pitt and Katie Holmes have been sighted. It has the decor of a waiting hall and is often crowded and slightly hectic, but the pizzas and the tiramisu are still worth it.
Lovely little vintage cafe. While drinks and cakes are decent, but not extraordinary for Mitte, the decor is really cute and it is very quiet. A good place to relax and read a magazine or book.
Good breakfast and playground next to the restaurant.

A small and lively cafe in the style of the 20s. There is a terrace on the river in summer. Their German cheesecake (with Quark and therefore lighter than the American version) comes especially recommended.
